reports.report: I analyzed the condition for an integer $m \ge 100$ to be colorful. A candy configuration is colorful if it contains at least 99 flavors in every group of 100 consecutive candies. For $m > 100$, this implies that each window of 100 candies must contain exactly one "repeat" (a candy whose flavor is the same as another in that window). The number of such repeats is $m - 99$. Each repeat $j$ at a distance $\delta_j$ covers $100 - \delta_j$ windows. For the condition to be satisfied, the sum of these window counts must be at least $m$, i.e., $\sum_{j=1}^{m-99} (100 - \delta_j) \ge m$. Since $\delta_j \ge 1$, we have $100 - \delta_j \le 99$, so we need $99(m-99) \ge m$, which simplifies to $99m - 9801 \ge m \implies 98m \ge 9801 \implies m \ge 100.01$. This implies that for $m > 100$, $m$ is colorful if $m \ge 101$. For $m=100$, the number of repeats is $100 - 99 = 1$. This one repeat can cover at most $100 - 1 = 99$ windows. However, there are 100 windows in the circle of 100 candies. Thus, $m=100$ is not colorful. For $m < 100$, $m$ is not colorful because it is impossible to have 99 flavors with fewer than 99 candies. Thus, the largest non-colorful integer is 100.

args.report: I analyzed the condition for an integer $m \ge 100$ to be colorful. A candy configuration is colorful if it contains at least 99 flavors in every group of 100 consecutive candies. For $m > 100$, this implies that each window of 100 candies must contain exactly one "repeat" (a candy whose flavor is the same as another in that window). The number of such repeats is $m - 99$. Each repeat $j$ at a distance $\delta_j$ covers $100 - \delta_j$ windows. For the condition to be satisfied, the sum of these window counts must be at least $m$, i.e., $\sum_{j=1}^{m-99} (100 - \delta_j) \ge m$. Since $\delta_j \ge 1$, we have $100 - \delta_j \le 99$, so we need $99(m-99) \ge m$, which simplifies to $99m - 9801 \ge m \implies 98m \ge 9801 \implies m \ge 100.01$. This implies that for $m > 100$, $m$ is colorful if $m \ge 101$. For $m=100$, the number of repeats is $100 - 99 = 1$. This one repeat can cover at most $100 - 1 = 99$ windows. However, there are 100 windows in the circle of 100 candies. Thus, $m=100$ is not colorful. For $m < 100$, $m$ is not colorful because it is impossible to have 99 flavors with fewer than 99 candies. Thus, the largest non-colorful integer is 100.
